tips.title: Cloudflare's Clef: the open-weight decision model
tips.summary: Cloudflare released Clef (27B) and Clef-flash (9B), its first in-house-trained models: open-weight (Apache 2.0) "decision models" that return per-option probabilities instead of generating text, aimed at the hot path of agentic workflows — routing, triage, escalation. The HN thread (626 pts, 217 comments) was split between awe at the speed of commoditization and skepticism: "open weights, not open source," and real-user tests showing Clef slower than Jev in production, contradicting vendor latency claims.

tips.title: book-to-skill: turn any technical book into a Claude Code skill
tips.summary: A five-month-old open-source project with 33,700 GitHub stars turns technical books — or any structured prose — into "agent skills": structured, on-demand knowledge bundles any AI coding agent can load while you work. It extracts clean text locally, then has your agent distill it into chapter files, a glossary, patterns, and a cheatsheet — claiming 24–51× fewer tokens per query than dumping the book into context. Despite the star count, public discussion is remarkably thin: one quiet HN post, no notable blog or YouTube coverage — the reception shows mainly in stars, awesome-list inclusion, and a growing family of derivative skills.

tips.title: Cloudflare's Pi harness: durable agents on the Agents SDK
tips.summary: Cloudflare announced first-class support for Earendil's Pi agent harness in the Agents SDK via a new PiHarness "Lifecycle capability," letting developers run long-lived, crash-resilient agents inside Durable Objects so work is durably persisted even when interrupted mid-turn. The integration combines Pi 1.0, the experimental Pi Durable framework, and the SDK's Lifecycle primitives — framed as the first step toward supporting third-party agent harnesses generally. Public discussion of the Cloudflare entry itself is thin; the buzz is concentrated on the Pi 1.0 / Pi Durable launch from the day before, which topped Hacker News.

tips.title: Big model, cheap decider: what the evidence says on Opus 5.5 + Jev, Codex Sol + Jev, and OpenAI's Decisions API
tips.summary: Beyond the hype on Opus 5.5 + Jev, Codex Sol + Jev, and Sol + OpenAI's Decisions API: the evidence says the winning pattern is one big model to think, one cheap model to decide, and plain code to enforce — with Jev matching Opus 5.5 at ~400x the cost on 216 real emails, question atomization worth 32 points of accuracy on the phishing bench (62.6% → 95%), and early tests showing Jev faster, cheaper, and more accurate on judgment calls than OpenAI's new Luna-based Decisions API. The catch: confidence numbers must be calibrated on your own labels, and the decision model never grants permissions.

tips.title: Nadella announces Microsoft-Decision-1: Microsoft enters the decision-model race
tips.summary: Satya Nadella announced Microsoft-Decision-1: a purpose-built model that scores fixed choices (yes/no, multiple-choice, ratings, rubric grading) via a structured API instead of generating text — aimed at routing, classification, verification, and agent workflow control. Microsoft claims top accuracy across 36 benchmarks, 4.5× faster than its closest rival and 35× faster than GPT-6 Sol on structured decisions, at $0.042 per million input tokens. Early developer reaction is cautiously positive, with independent testers confirming it's competitive with TypeSafe's Jev — while skeptics note all the benchmarks are Microsoft's own.

tips.title: Flue: the TypeScript framework for durable AI agents
tips.summary: Flue is an open-source TypeScript framework for building durable, autonomous AI agents, launched May 1, 2026 by Astro co-creator Fred Schott's team. Agents are functions marked with a 'use agent' directive, composed with a React-like hooks API; it's built on the Pi harness, supports any Pi model provider, and deploys to Node, Cloudflare Workers, CI, and edge runtimes — with durability from an append-only event log. The repo (withastro/flue, Apache-2.0) has 8,443 stars and is actively maintained. Reception: a lively but skeptical HN launch thread, and Firecrawl calling it a 'framework moment' alongside Vercel's Eve — though public discussion beyond the launch is thin.

tips.title: Vercel's Eve: the 'Next.js for agents'
tips.summary: Vercel's Eve is an open-source (Apache-2.0), TypeScript-first agent framework launched June 17, 2026 at Vercel Ship, pitched as "Next.js for agents." An agent is a directory — agent.ts, instructions.md, tools/, skills/, subagents/, channels/, schedules/, connections/ — with durability, sandboxing, human-in-the-loop approvals, tracing, and evals built in. The repo (github.com/vercel/eve) has 5,513 stars and is still in public beta. Vs Flue: near-identical shape, but deployment is the fundamental difference — Eve is Vercel-first, Flue is multi-cloud. Discussion is warm but thin: bloggers validate the design, builders flag lock-in, and hands-on adoption is still early.

tips.title: Gemini 4 Argon goes global — in Antigravity for Ultra subscribers only
tips.summary: Google's Antigravity account posted on launch day for Gemini 4 Argon, now globally available — inside Antigravity (desktop, CLI, Android Studio Canary) for Google AI Ultra subscribers only. Google also opened applications for 10,000 scientists to get six months free at Antigravity's highest usage tier. API pricing is $2/$10 per million tokens intro, rising to $4/$20 after November 30, 2026, with a 1M unified token limit. Early reaction centers on access: a gradual rollout, Pro-vs-Ultra as the fault line, and independent benchmarks cooler than Google's claims (Artificial Analysis 53, tied with Astra, behind Opus 5.5 at 58).

tips.title: All-In interviews Martin Shkreli: quantum shorts, big pharma, and prison
tips.summary: The All-In account's Oct 12 post almost certainly announces the new ~25-minute interview episode with Martin Shkreli — "Big Pharma's Blind Spot, Betting Against Quantum & What Prison Taught Him." Shkreli on why quantum computing is "a one-trick business" and why he's shorting it; drugs big pharma prices too cheap; AI in drug discovery; and what prison taught him. Secondary summaries add: his quantum short has lost millions, photonic matrix multiplication could make current GPUs "scrap metal within two decades," he calls Dario Amodei a "fear-monger," and predicts no AI-relevant drug in 10 years. Coverage is thin — no HN, Reddit, or major press.

tips.title: 1Password for Agents: AI agents that sign in without ever seeing your password
tips.summary: 1Password launched 1Password for Agents (Oct 22, 2026): personal AI agents can sign into your accounts without ever seeing your passwords. The agent identifies itself with a unique digital key, you approve the specific login on your device, and 1Password fills the credential directly into the site; MFA codes go through the same channel, and access is per-session with no carryover. Included free in Individual/Family plans. Muse (Meta) and Grok Bot roll out first; Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work/dots, and Townie are coming soon, with Browserbase, Perplexity, Ramp, and others building. Reaction is split: partners (Muse team, KERNEL) are enthusiastic, while security analysts note the guarantee ends at sign-in — the signed-in session, not the password, becomes the risk.
